historical_references.reference: The name Azwan is derived from the Arabic word for bountiful or generous, 'az-zawan', which was used to describe the fertile land along the banks of the Euphrates River in Iraq. This region was a center of Islamic civilization during the Abbasid Caliphate (750-1258 CE).

Azwan was also the name of a major tributary that flowed into the Arabian Sea, and was an important source of water for the ancient city of Aden in Yemen. During the Aden Sultanate period (1538-1637 CE), Azwan was a prosperous port city that played a significant role in the Indian Ocean trade.
